thread.title: Inspired by Apple, Robinhood takes greater control of its destiny with buildout

author: Mark Calvey
title: Inspired by Apple, Robinhood takes greater control of its destiny with buildout
text: – Senior Reporter, San Francisco Business Times Oct 10, 2018, 9:30am PDT Menlo Park-based Robinhood said Wednesday that it has built a key element of its trading operations to have more control over customers’ experience with the online brokerage as well as have the ability to add features and services rapidly. The company spent two years and an untold sum on the engineering and regulatory challenges that came with the creation of Clearing by Robinhood, which will act as the company's in-house clearing house. Banks have traditionally "cleared" transactions, acting as intermediaries to complete them on behalf of the buyer and the seller. By creating its own clearing arm, Robinhood will save money on fees, which it can then pass on to its customers. Robinhood said Clearing by Robinhood is the only clearing operation built from scratch over the past decade. That means Robinhood won’t be hampered by a common industry hurdle in financial services: legacy technology. “We’re taking all the ownership in house. Customers will see a huge difference,” Vlad Tenev , Robinhood co-founder and co-CEO, told the San Francisco Business Times. “It will increase our product velocity. It will help scale Robinhood to support tens of millions of customers and expand into new verticals. “It’s like Apple creating their own chips,” Tenev said in discussing why it was so important for Robinhood to have its own clearing operations. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) made national headlines almost a decade ago when it decided to design its own computer chips, which it saw as a way to create exclusive features, protect its work from rivals and incorporate innovations faster, the Wall Street Journal reported at the time. Clearing by Robinhood will handle the settlement of customers’ transactions involving stocks, options and cryptocurrencies. Robinhood said its own clearing operations will also cut costs and boost revenue for the company, which is said to be preparing for an IPO . The brokerage has raised $539 million from some of Silicon Valley's best known investors, including DST Global, NEA, Index Ventures, Thrive Capital, Sequoia Capital, Kleiner Perkins and Capital G, formerly Google Capital. Robinhood, founded in 2013 by Baiju Bhatt and Tenev offering commission-free stock trades, struck gold with margin lending, which is offered as part of an upgraded service aptly named Robinhood Gold. The company’s margin lending is priced as a monthly fee that is often considerably less than what Charles Schwab (NYSE: SCHW), E-Trade (NASDAQ: ETFC) or other rivals charge. Robinhood said it will independently clear and settle transactions as well as custody assets for all of its customers, which Robinhood said today now totals 6 million investors, making it the fastest-growing brokerage. The new clearing operation means Robinhood will no longer depend on outside firm Apex Clearing Corp. On the regulatory front, Clearing by Robinhood required the formation of a new entity, Robinhood Securities, in 2016. Plus, the company had to receive regulatory approvals from three different agencies. Robinhood also said its new clearing operation includes an internal customer dashboard, allowing the company’s customer service representatives to have more information on a customer’s transactions. “We’ll now have direct insight into a customer’s account,” said Christine Hall , the product lead for Clearing by Robinhood. The brokerage also plans to roll out redesigned account statements and tax documents that will be easier to understand, using simpler language. Robinhood has more than 250 employees, with about 70 employees in its regional headquarters in Lake Mary, Fla., near Orlando. The company’s Florida employees focus on brokerage operations, compliance and customer support. – Senior Reporter, San Francisco Business Times Oct 10, 2018, 9:30am PDT Thursday, October 18, 2018 Silicon Valley Fast Private Awards CEOs and executive staff gather to find out where their companies rank on this year's list of Silicon Valley's Fastest Growing Private Companies.
